chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: If you find in the expiation only one man or two men, then repeat [the payment] upon them until you complete ten. Give them [their share] today, then give them [their share] tomorrow.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤَمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.الكَفَّارَة: Expiation (penalty or charity to atone for a specific act or omission)

ai.seo_question: How to fulfill the requirement of ten recipients for expiation if only a few are available?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) via Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), clarifying the flexibility in the number of recipients for *kaffarah* (expiation) when the pool of eligible poor is limited. The ruling permits concentrating the distribution on fewer individuals by repeating the grant, thereby ensuring the spiritual obligation is fulfilled even in scarcity, a principle widely accepted in Shia jurisprudence for various expiations.
